item.title: Galway road fatalities up from five to 18 despite one-third cut in crashes
item.description: DESPITE an overall decrease in serious road traffic accidents across Galway in 2025, there were 18 fatalities recorded in the county over the course of the year – an increase of 360% as compared to 2024 – the latest Garda figures have revealed. item.title: Minister promises renewed focus on tackling road safety
item.description: The Galway TD and Minister of State with responsibility for Road Safety has vowed that 2026 will be a year of renewed focus for his Department on tackling fatalities on Irish roads. item.title: Tractors Light Up for Iggy
item.description: More than 210 tractors and 13 trucks took part in the Light Up for Iggy Christmas Tractor Run at Galway Plaza, as families and the farming community came together to honour the memory of Iggy Daly and raise funds for Cholangiocarcinoma Ireland. item.title: Solicitor is welcomed to court
item.description: One of Galway’s newest solicitors has been welcomed to the profession at a sitting of a District Court. Conor Ruane, originally from Monivea but now living with his family in Crumlin, Ballyglunin, is practicing with the long established McDarby and Co Solicitors in Ballinrobe. item.title: Quota cuts leave fishing sector in a state of peril
item.description: Coastal communities in Conamara dependent on fishing face an uncertain year after the European Union slashed quotas for Ireland in 2026 – a move described as ‘catastrophic’ by the industry. item.title: Electric finally tips the balance in Galway’s new car sales
item.description: The number of new cars that are partly or fully run by electricity made up the majority of sales in Galway during 2025 — for the first time ever. Electric and hybrid electric vehicles accounted for 2,879 of the total new car sales of 5,152 here last year.
